title: Oncall + Demo SDK quicklabs and runbook notes
content:
Purpose: lightweight, reproducible lab recipes engineers can run in 10–30 minutes for an oncall triage session or customer-facing demo. This doc is a sketchbook: operational checks, demo scripts, minimal repro steps, and 'what to say' for demos. Intended audience: SDK maintainers, oncall rotation, solutions eng demo runners.

Structure: quick checklist -> smoke labs -> deep triage pointers -> demo script -> postmortem checklist -> open questions/TODOs. Keep each lab self-contained; prefer commands that work with local env or a sandbox project.

Quick checklist (pre-run):
- Confirm credentials: export REDWOOD_API_KEY (use demo token)
- CLI version: redwood --version >= 0.9.7 (breaking telemetry flags changed in 0.9.5)
- Start local proxy if needed: ./tools/local-proxy --env demo --port 8080
- Telemetry window: open Console -> route "sdk-demo" -> last 30m
- Prepare fallback model: text-compact-1 on standby for latency issues

Smoke lab A: First-request happy path (10–12 min)
- Goal: show zero-to-first-response with streaming and structured output.
- Steps:
  1) git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk-examples.git && cd sdk-examples/quicklabs/oncall-demo
  2) cp .env.sample .env && set REDWOOD_API_KEY in .env
  3) python3 -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
  4) pip install -r requirements.txt
  5) python demo_streaming.py --model text-bison-1 --prompt-file prompts/hello-world.txt
- Expected: streaming chunks appear in terminal within 350–600ms for local-sim, or 200–400ms for hosted.
- Common failures and quick fixes:
  - TimeoutError at connect: proxy not running or wrong port -> run proxy, check env ports.
  - 401 Unauthorized: wrong token; confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY is demo token.
  - Empty stream: check prompt file encoding (utf-8), remove weird zero-width chars.

Smoke lab B: Embeddings + similarity fallback (12–20 min)
- Goal: show token-cost dashboard and a cheap fallback via lower-cost embedding + rerank.
- Steps:
  1) node quick_embed.js --dataset sample-kb.json --index local
  2) curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/queries" -d '{"query":"what is our SLA?","mode":"rerank"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY"
- Observability checks: view Console -> Optimize -> embedding-cost by route; check token breakdown for rerank route.
- Pitfalls: small index degeneracy: tune k from 10 -> 5 if results noisy.

Oncall triage heuristics (rapid):
- First 60s: confirm scope (single route? multiple routes?).
- Reproduce quickly in local-sim (reduce variables): same prompt, model, headers.
- If latency spikes: capture p99 traces (Console -> Observability -> traces -> filter route). Look for queueing vs GPU spend.
- Quick mitigation options (live):
  - switch traffic to fallback model via config: curl -X POST /v1/routes/{id}/override -d '{"model":"text-compact-1"}'
  - reduce batch_window (console) to prioritize latency for the affected route
  - enable function-level fail-open to return last-good cached response for read-only endpoints

Demo script (customer-focused, 8–10 min):
- Opening lines: "We'll start from a simple snippet that reads a support ticket and returns a triage suggestion. It takes ~20ms per token on the demo stack."
- Steps to run live:
  1) open quicklabs/oncall-demo/demo-notebook.ipynb (or demo_streaming.py for terminal)
  2) run cell 1: authenticate (show subtle token obfuscation)
  3) run cell 2: call summarize_ticket(prompt), show streaming highlight + structured JSON output
  4) run cell 3: flip to 'low-cost mode' (embedding + rerank) and show cost meter drop in Console
- Recovery script: if streaming stalls, refresh cell that calls model with --no-cache flag; if auth error, switch to recorded demo and narrate steps.

Debug commands and useful queries: (copy-paste friendly)
- curl request example with headers and streaming accept:
  curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
    -d '{"model":"text-seed-1","input":"Explain X"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Console trace quick-filter (internal): trace.service=sdk AND route=sdk-demo AND latency>200ms
- SQL-ish query for slow buckets: SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE route='sdk-demo' AND status!='200' AND created_at > now() - interval '1 hour';

Postmortem checklist (if demo or oncall incident):
- Save raw SDK logs (tools/log-exporter) and attach to ticket.
- Snapshot Console -> Model -> version + kernel selection at time of incident.
- Mark whether this was infra, model, or prompt-quality. Add to incident board PROJ-2314 if reproducible.
- Draft a short follow-up note for customers: what happened, brief root cause, mitigation, ETA for full fix.

Short people's guide: who to call during a live demo
- Primary: oncall-developers slack channel (#oncall-sdk)
- Escalation: Marco Liu (eng-sre) then Priya (product-owner for SDK docs)
- Backup: solutions-eng rotation lead (Evan C.)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add a one-click demo script that auto-creates a sandbox API key and route (worth a spike) -> spike owner: Priya (ETA 2025-03-14)
- Improve recorded-demo fallback: include a 'canned traces' view in Console so demo always shows telemetry graphs
- Harden README for demo labs: include known flaky networks and proxy instructions.

Notes to self:
- Keep labs < 4 external deps (pip/node) and use ephemeral tokens.
- Add a "panic button" section in notebook that switches to recorded outputs and shows 'why we switched'.

Appendix: sample check phrases for demos
- "If you see a spike, we'll switch to a lower-cost/low-latency variant and continue — this keeps your UX seamless."
- "This route is instrumented — you can inspect token-level cost in the Console after this call."

End of doc. Save as living notes; prefer incremental PRs to examples repo (see linked PR).
